title: CRLR/373/2019 of DILSHAD Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
CRLR No. 373 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Kundan Singh Negi, Advocate for
the revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, A.G.A. along with Mr.
Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for the State.
The present revision has been preferred
by the revisionist/husband, whereby, he has
challenged the order dated 21.05.2019 as
passed by the Family Court, Haridwar, by
virtue of which while considering the
application paper no. 10A for the grant of
interim maintenance the Family Court after
considering the fact that the revisionist and the
respondent no. 2 they have been married
according to the muslim rituals on 18.03.2007,
but there is some family dispute, which has
arisen on account of which the respondent no. 2
had to file an application under Section 125 of
Cr.P.C. before the Family Court, Haridwar, for
claiming a maintenance of Rs. 3,000/- per
month.
For the said purpose she has contended in
the pleading that as far as the
revisionist/husband is concerned, he is having a
sufficient land and is running a dairy from
where his income is pleaded to be atleast Rs. 3
lakhs per month. However, the Family Court at
an interim stage, considering the fact that the
marriage is still subsisting, had awarded a
maintenance of Rs. 3,000/- per month to
respondent no. 2.
During the course of arguments, the
learned counsel for the revisionist has
expressed his desire that he is willing to take
back his wife, keep her with herself and
discharge his matrimonial obligation.
Considering the said inclination, the
Family Court is requested to call upon both the

parties and make an effort for mediation so that
they may be brought together in a family, but as
far as the grant of interim maintenance is
concerned, considering the quantum of amount,
which has been awarded, i.e. Rs. 3,000/- per
month, being quite reasonable, this Court
declines to interfere with the order dated
21.05.2019.
A request has been made by the learned
counsel for the revisionist that this Court may
also issue an appropriate direction to the Family
Court, Haridwar, to consider the application
under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. on its own merits
as expeditiously as possible so that the
controversy between the revisionist and
respondent no. 2 may be resolved at the earliest.
Considering the intention and the
circumstances which are prevailing while
dismissing this revision, this Court requests the
Family Court, Haridwar, to make an earnest
effort for mediation and also to ensure that the
application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. is
decided as expeditiously as possible but not
later than three months from the date of
production of certified copy of this order.
Subject to the above liberty, the revision
stands dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 10.07.2019
Pooja
